paper_title: Interleaving Retrieval with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for   Knowledge-Intensive Multi-Step Questions
caption: Number of questions, out of 40, where CoT generated by GPT3 using different methods has at least 1 factual error. Factual errors: < OneR < NoR.
model_annotation: This grouped bar chart illustrates the number of questions containing factual errors across four distinct datasets evaluated using three different methods. The horizontal category axis displays the datasets in the following order: HotpotQA, 2WikiMQA, MuSiQue, and IIRC, without an explicit axis label. The vertical value axis features a linear scale representing the count of errors, ranging from 0 to 40, with numeric tick labels positioned at regular intervals of 5. While the vertical axis lacks a formal title, an outlined text box in the upper left corner specifies "Factual Errors." For each dataset on the horizontal axis, three vertically oriented bars are grouped side-by-side, differentiated by color and pattern according to a legend in the upper right. The legend identifies "NoR QA" as orange bars with a faint grid pattern, "OneR QA" as red bars with a stippled dot pattern, and "IRCoT QA" as dark blue bars with diagonal stripes. Exact numerical values are explicitly annotated directly above each corresponding bar for visual emphasis. In the HotpotQA group, NoR QA has a value of 15, OneR QA is 10, and IRCoT QA is 5, which represents the shortest bar in the chart. For 2WikiMQA, the values are 29 for NoR QA—the tallest bar overall—23 for OneR QA, and 14 for IRCoT QA. In the MuSiQue category, the bars show values of 28 for NoR QA, 27 for OneR QA, and 23 for IRCoT QA. Finally, for the IIRC dataset, NoR QA indicates a value of 15, OneR QA is 14, and IRCoT QA is 11. Across all four horizontal categories, the bars within each group visually descend in height from left to right, strictly ordered as NoR QA, OneR QA, and IRCoT QA.
